UN World Population Prospects 2024 period life tables for 2023

Source: R/data-mortality-regions.R
mortality_regions.Rd

A selection of official 2023 period estimates, with single-year ages 0 through 99 and an open 100+ interval, for 67 countries or areas and 28 geographic aggregates. These are model-based estimates for a reference period, not observed individual lifetimes or cohort forecasts.

Usage

mortality_regions

Format

A tibble with 28,785 rows and 21 columns:

location_code, location

UN WPP location identifier and name. For countries and areas the identifier is the numeric M49 code; aggregates use WPP identifiers, which need not be M49 codes.

iso3

ISO alpha-3 code for countries and areas; missing for aggregates.

level, region, subregion

Selection level (country, world, major region or subregion) and geographic grouping. Missing grouping labels denote levels where the grouping does not apply.

year, sex

Calendar year (2023) and sex category ("female", "male" or "both").

x, age_interval, age_span, open_interval

Starting age in years, original interval label, interval width in years (-1 is the original open-interval marker), and an explicit open-interval flag.

mx

Central mortality rate, deaths per person-year.

qx, px

Death and survival probabilities over the interval, in base 1. At 100+, 1 and 0 refer to the open interval.

lx, dx

Survivors at the start and published deaths in the interval, per initial 100,000 lives.

Lx, Tx

Person-years in the interval and total remaining person-years, per initial 100,000 lives.

ex, ax

Remaining life expectancy and mean years lived in the interval by those who die, in years.

Source

United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024, complete period life tables, 2023 estimates. https://population.un.org/wpp/. Data attribution: United Nations, CC BY 3.0 IGO (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/igo/). This package subsets and renames columns, adds geographic selection labels and an open-interval flag, and preserves the numeric values.

Details

Keys are location_code, year, sex and x. No numeric source values were rescaled, interpolated or replaced. Rounding can cause small differences between the published probabilities and ratios of published survivor counts. For valuation from survivor counts, supply only x and lx from a single table and choose a supported finite horizon. Do not interpret 100+ as a one-year interval or infer an age of extinction from it. In particular, the published open-interval dx in the 84 aggregate rows differs from lx * qx; it is retained as published, without treating it as a one-year decrement or forcing the identity at that boundary.

Examples

col <- subset(mortality_regions, location_code == 170L & sex == "both",
              select = c(x, lx))
t_px(col, x = 65, t = 5)
#> [1] 0.933984
